headline: Easy-run efficiency is holding firmly across the recent 20 km and 11 km work, but with a 580 km self-supported crossing under three weeks out, the training still lacks anything resembling loaded-pack carrying or sustained climbing. That gap, not fitness, is the story worth sitting with right now.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The recent block sits squarely in a build phase — running volume across the last four weeks is well up on the prior four, and the runs themselves are clustering in the lower HR bands at comparable paces, which is a genuinely encouraging efficiency picture. Strength has stayed present but light lately, with shorter functional sessions rather than the hour-long blocks from earlier in the month; that's a sensible trade against the rising run load rather than a lapse. Steps remain high even on rest days, so background time-on-feet is doing real work here. The one figure to actively disregard is the cardio-load "detraining" status — it reads zero strain against a healthy tolerance, which given the volume you're actually running is clearly an artefact, not a signal. Sleep has been erratic, with several short and a couple of unscored nights, but that stays in the supporting column.
sections.trends: The year-to-date comparison is the headline shape: you're carrying nearly five times the distance you had by this date last year, and the recent four-week jump reflects a deliberate ramp rather than noise. The 12-week average masks how front-loaded the recent volume is. This building shape fits year-round hybrid readiness well, and the ramp is steep enough that the next natural move is consolidation rather than another step up — especially with a long self-supported effort approaching.
